While some players have demonstrated patience and a willingness to actually become informed as to what their respective nation's capabilities are, others seem to be claiming territories and simply acting in a way doesn't make any sense. Yes, this sub is meant to be somewhat loose on the rules and allow players to roleplay and be creative, but players still need to be cognizant of what is reasonable for their nations to do. So here are some suggestions:

  1. Research your country - Wikipedia is your friend. This should give you a good overview with some useful information, backstory, history, etc. Another good suggestion is the CIA World Factbook (search for it).
  2. While you should be free to be creative with your persona, policies, ideologies, relationships with other countries, etc, you should not feel so free when it comes to your nation's resources, manpower, and so on. The reason is because if everyone was to completely throw reality to the wind the game would quickly deteriorate.

With that said, be reasonable and use common sense. To name a specific (arbitrary) example, it's perfectly fine that someone would, say, claim Atlantis. But it's completely crazy that they would, even within a few years, have an enormous navy, much less actually invade anything as they don't even have citizens or industry or anything that might support any kind of military power.

Addendum: For those out there who read that while nodding their heads, so long as you're nice and down to Earth, don't be afraid to say so in those threads too. Because of the rule style, the mods need us to gauge what is generally considered reasonable.

Vivian Plays #1 - All Time Favorites - Submit Your Reviews Now!

Time for the first curator pick for Vivian Plays! The theme for this week is All Time Favorites and just this once, we'll be picked the top TEN reviews, not just the top indie and AAA. You can review any game you like regardless of genre or cost, as long as it's available on Steam. Make sure you review the rules and feel free to ask if you have any questions. Also, whether you submit a review or not, BE SURE TO VOTE.

This will go for the entire weekend and will end Sunday at midnight (PST). After that, we will take all the reviews and update this to reflect the winning reviews and the giveaway winner.

Rules of Review

1.Include any relevant disclosures. Obviously.

2.Your review has to be a REVIEW. You can't just name a game. You can't just describe a game. Tell us WHY the game is good. Try for at least a paragraph or more but we don't necessarily have a minimum.

3.Your review will be posted in full on the curator list or with an archived link to it, and you'll be credited based on your Reddit name. If you'd prefer to be credited as someone else, let us know. (Also, on this note, please do not plagiarize your reviews...)

4.DON'T SHILL VOTES. I shouldn't have to say this but seriously, don't go telling your friends "hey vote for mine" or making multiple accounts or anything like that. If we catch people shilling votes or if we find out you left out a crucial disclosure, your entry will be disqualified. This is pretty much the only way we'll disqualify reviews, but we're also not making exceptions on this. Don't do it.

5.Recommended games have to be on Steam, unfortunately, We may look into other listing programs that will allow ALL games, but for now, just Steam. (NOTE: If you post a review and the game isn't on Steam, it won't disqualify you from the giveaway, just means we can't use the review on the curator list).

6.This is less a rule and more a suggestion, as we can't track this in any way, but use downvotes sparingly. Don't downvote a post just because you dislike a game, but base it on the quality of the review, if you must. Otherwise, use your voting power to upvote games you like, without necessarily cancelling out the votes of others. Again, we have no way to enforce this, but consider this just a recommendation, for the sake of fair sport.

Giveaway Rules

1.You must submit a review to be eligible for the giveaway. Everyone who enters gets a chance.

2.The giveaway for this one will be the top voted indie game.

3.We will contact you to get your Steam account in order to gift it to you.

4.You can do what you want with the game. We would prefer if you don't sell it but we won't stop you.

5.If you don't want the game, let us know, and someone else will be picked.

Disclosures

Volunteers (right now just me and /u/frakingalldaylong) can't submit anything to be put on the list. No reviews from us, and our comments can only be meta (in relation to the contest itself, not the reviews). We can vote, but that's about it.
